cd cli && GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go test -c -o TASK_TEMP/sandbox-linux-amd64.test ./internal/assurance/sandbox

result.authorization: a successful probe creates one private time-bounded authorization; copies share synchronized consumption state, so replay or expiry stops before launch
result.correlation: the run requires the exact probed Codex identity, configuration, probe binding, posture digest, helper inode and bytes, and private Codex state path, inode, and digest
result.processOwnership: each launch receives a new process group; timeout, cancellation, output-cap, nonzero exit, and successful parent exit all perform bounded post-wait group-absence verification
result.output: stdout and stderr are independently stream-capped at caller-declared positive limits up to 16 MiB and truncation is explicit
result.duration: the caller context and a positive run timeout capped at one hour cancel the process group; timeout evidence remains set even if cleanup also fails
result.exit: normal and nonzero application exit codes remain bounded result evidence; launch, timeout, cancellation, output, and cleanup failures retain distinct closed reasons
result.environment: the process receives an exact constructed environment and never os.Environ; SE-03-07 owns the final expected-present and expected-absent policy
result.tests: focused count-10, process-leak count-100, package, race, all-assurance, vet, format, and Darwin/Linux/Windows compile-only checks passed
result.independentReview: approved the one-shot/state-bound launch and classified max-process enforcement as a separate mandatory Phase 03 exit gate; no reviewer writes

limits: This task proves source and local test behavior. It did not execute Codex, the native sandbox, a project command, the Mastra SDK, a provider/model request, production credentials/endpoints, or an external control-plane operation.

Process-group ownership and verified cleanup are not a maximum-process-count budget. The Phase 03 exit and support-tuple qualification remain blocked until maxProcesses has real enforcement evidence; no polling-based or cleanup-only surrogate is claimed.

Darwin and Linux use process-group semantics. The other-platform implementation exists only for compilation and the exported Codex runner rejects every platform except the exact Darwin/arm64 candidate.
SE-03-08 still owns native denial/config evidence normalization, and SE-03-09 owns full run-owned process, socket, path, and outside-sentinel cleanup evidence.
